sabrina::spec-writer — P4.B3 destructive.question: When `destructive_actions` is absent from `sabrina.toml` entirely (older config), should the allow-list default-deny or default-allow?

options.label: Default-deny on missing
options.desc: Empty list = "deny all destructive." Older configs upgrading inherit the safer posture. Three explicit flips (`[tools.X] enabled`, `[automation] destructive_actions`, `[tools] enabled`) needed to enable.

options.label: Default-allow on missing
options.desc: Distinguishes "user hasn't decided" from "user denied." Silently allows destructive tools on configs that haven't been re-audited — opposite of safety-primitive posture.

recommendation.rationale: Safety primitive default-deny matches CLAUDE.md "no silent failures" — a missing field that leaks open on upgrade is exactly the case to avoid.

sabrina::spec-writer — P4.B3 destructive.question: Should `destructive_actions` entries match tool names by exact match, glob (fnmatch), or regex?

options.label: Exact match
options.desc: `name == entry`. Each new destructive tool requires an explicit allow-list entry. Tightest posture; re-audit is the design intent.

options.label: Glob (fnmatch)
options.desc: `fnmatch.fnmatchcase`. `send_*` auto-allows a future `send_text` that didn't exist when the user wrote the toml — leaks forward in time.

options.label: Regex (re.fullmatch)
options.desc: Most expressive. Cost: users learn regex; leak-forward-in-time risk compounds; complexity that no current tool needs.

recommendation.rationale: Forcing a per-tool re-audit on every new destructive verb is precisely what the safety primitive should buy.

sabrina::spec-writer — P4.A1 avatar arch.question: Should the avatar window use full Qt click-through, or per-pixel opaque-regions-accept-clicks via Windows native flags?

options.label: Full window click-through
options.desc: `WA_TransparentForMouseEvents` always on. Simplest; smallest Windows-native surface; no per-pixel transparency code. Kill targets live elsewhere (tray, supervisor CLI, P4.B1 hotkey).

options.label: Per-pixel opaque-clicks
options.desc: `SetWindowLong` + `WS_EX_LAYERED` + `WS_EX_TRANSPARENT` to let opaque regions accept clicks (e.g. a kill-button on the avatar itself). More fragile; needs ctypes/pywin32.

recommendation.rationale: Kill targets already exist outside the avatar window; per-pixel transparency buys nothing v1 needs and adds a Windows-only fragile surface.

sabrina::spec-writer — P4.A1 avatar arch.question: Should the avatar subscribe to the event bus in-process via `qasync`, or run as a side-process subscriber via local IPC?

options.label: In-process via qasync
options.desc: Avatar runs alongside the voice loop in one process; direct `bus.subscribe`. Zero IPC overhead; Qt event loop co-exists with asyncio via qasync (well-maintained, Windows wheels).

options.label: Side-process via local IPC
options.desc: Separate Python process; IPC via local TCP / named pipe / stdin-stdout JSONL. Crash isolation; ~1ms-class latency; doubles process-management overhead.

recommendation.rationale: Supervisor primitive (acd6725) already provides process-level crash isolation cheaper than IPC; in-process keeps the bus contract single-shape.

sabrina::spec-writer — P4.A2 avatar PyQt.question: Should PyQt6 (~50 MB wheel) + `qasync` ship as core deps, an optional extra, or a vendored lazy-import?

options.label: Optional extra
options.desc: Install via `uv pip install -e .[avatar]`. Pure voice-loop users skip the wheel. Matches ROADMAP "nice-to-have" framing.

options.label: Vendored lazy-import

recommendation.rationale: Avatar is explicitly nice-to-have in ROADMAP §6; gating the 50 MB wheel behind an extra keeps the voice-loop minimal install honest.
